_meta.source: AIGP original governance checklist for agentic AI use-cases
_meta.note: All items are original AIGP wording. No third-party publication text is reproduced.

sections.title: Tool & connection access
sections.intent: The agent can only reach the tools, credentials, and destinations it genuinely needs.

items.text: Every tool or connector the agent can invoke is on an explicit allowlist.
The agent holds no standing or ambient credentials beyond its least-privilege scope.
The data-egress destinations the agent can reach are enumerated and restricted.
Tool permissions are re-reviewed whenever the agent's scope changes.

sections.title: Action logging & traceability
sections.intent: What the agent did, and why, can be reconstructed after the fact.

items.text: Agent actions, tool calls, and intermediate reasoning steps are logged.
Handoffs between agents, or between agent and human, are recorded and replayable.
Logs are tamper-evident and retained per policy.
A specific run can be reconstructed end-to-end from the recorded trail.

sections.title: Human oversight & stage-gates
sections.intent: Humans stay in control of consequential and irreversible actions.

items.text: Critical or irreversible outputs require explicit human sign-off before taking effect.
A documented kill-switch can halt the agent mid-run.
Autonomy thresholds — what the agent may do unsupervised — are written down.
The human reviewer is given enough context to approve or reject meaningfully.

sections.title: Evaluation vs baseline
sections.intent: The workflow is measured against a known-good baseline before and after launch.

items.text: Workflow accuracy is benchmarked against a human baseline before launch.
Scope or autonomy is only widened after a passing re-benchmark.
Evaluation covers adversarial and edge-case inputs, not just the happy path.
Evaluation results are recorded and dated.

sections.title: Operational resilience
sections.intent: The agent degrades safely and stays within operational bounds.

items.text: A fallback path exists for model or agent outage or degraded performance.
Performance degradation is detected and alerts a named owner.
Rate, cost, and loop limits bound the agent's runaway behaviour.
Recovery from a failed run leaves downstream systems in a consistent state.

sections.title: Accountability & ownership
sections.intent: A human is answerable for the agent and its outputs.

items.text: A named human owner is accountable for each agent-produced output.
The owner can explain how a given output was produced.
Roles and escalation paths for agent incidents are assigned.
The use-case has a documented purpose and approved operating boundaries.

sections.title: Data sourcing & output validation
sections.intent: Inputs are trustworthy and outputs are checked before they are relied upon.

items.text: Input data sources are defined, validated, and authorised for this use.
Review points exist before outputs enter systems of record.
Outputs are checked for sensitive-data leakage before release.
Source-data quality issues are detectable and surfaced.
